subject: physics
question_text: Find the scalar and vector products of two vectors a = (3i − 4j + 5k) and b = (−2i + j − 3k).

verification.note: Asked in TS March 2020 (Q14) — TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, Section B, 4 marks. appearances[] is left empty deliberately: a separate reviewed tagging pass fills that field from a reviewed mapping, so a hand-written entry here would read as an invented tag. The 1+1+2 split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Arithmetic hand-checked. Scalar product: a · b = (3)(−2) + (−4)(1) + (5)(−3) = −6 − 4 − 15 = −25. Vector product, expanding the determinant along the top row: i = (−4)(−3) − (5)(1) = 12 − 5 = 7; j = −[(3)(−3) − (5)(−2)] = −[−9 + 10] = −1; k = (3)(1) − (−4)(−2) = 3 − 8 = −5, so a × b = 7i − j − 5k. Perpendicularity check: a · (a × b) = 3(7) + (−4)(−1) + 5(−5) = 21 + 4 − 25 = 0.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The scalar product
lines: The scalar product multiplies the matching
components and adds the three products:
steps.margin_note: First mark. The number −25, with its minus sign.
steps.why: The scalar product pairs each component with the matching one and adds, so the result is a single number with no direction. All three products here are negative, which is why the sum is −25.
common_mistakes: Adding 6 + 4 + 15 and writing 25 without the minus sign.
Giving the scalar product a direction. It is one number, with no i, j or k.

reject: seven i minus j minus five k

steps.memory_tip: Matching components only: i with i, j with j, k with k. The answer is one number.

steps.label: The determinant
lines: The vector product is a determinant with
i, j, k on the top row, a next, b last:
Each group between the bars is one row.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The determinant written with a above b.
steps.why: The determinant is only the bookkeeping for the vector product. The order of the rows fixes the sign: a above b gives a × b, and swapping them gives b × a.
common_mistakes: Writing b in the second row and a in the third, which reverses every component.

recall.must_convey: That the vector product is the determinant with i, j, k on the top row, then a, then b.
accept: determinant with i j k on top
a in the second row and b in the third
reject: a dot b is minus twenty five

steps.memory_tip: Top row i, j, k. Second row a, third row b. That order fixes the sign of a × b.

steps.label: The vector product
lines: Expand along the top row. The j term
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. All three components, with the j term negative.
steps.why: Expanding along the top row alternates the signs +, −, +, so the j component carries an extra minus. That alternating sign is the only difference between this expansion and an ordinary sum of products.
common_mistakes: Expanding the j term without the extra minus sign, which gives +1 instead of −1.
Writing the k component as 3 + 8 = 11. The product (−4)(−2) is +8 and is subtracted.

accept: seven i minus j minus five k
seven i minus j minus five k vasthundi
reject: a dot b is minus twenty five

steps.memory_tip: Check it: a · (a × b) = 21 + 4 − 25 = 0. A vector product is perpendicular to both.

insider_note: Two answers are asked and both are marked — the number −25 and the vector 7i − j − 5k. The minus on the j component is where the marks go.
